parsedVerdict.reasoning: ReceivingService is an application/domain service in the business layer. It coordinates stock operations: receive() looks up an item and a bin, calls bin.put() and saves the bin. pick() takes stock from bins until the requested quantity is met, adds up what is on hand and calls item.needsReorder(). The actual rules live on the stock objects (Bin.put, Bin.take, Item.needsReorder), and failed lookups raise the domain error StockError. The file has no SQL, connection or transaction handling, HTTP or framework code. The private item()/bin() helpers and the loop in pick() build Item and Bin from raw record fields, and store({ ...bin }) passes a copy of the bin back to the table. That record conversion would ideally sit in a persistence repository, but it is a small amount of glue code, not real persistence logic, so it is not counted as a misplaced responsibility. Importing and injecting the concrete BinTable/ItemTable classes is a dependency-direction issue, which is out of scope for this rule.
